scenes.title: Cold open
narration: During the Bhaijauntia festival, women dance outside the temple of the mother goddess while praying for their brothers' longevity, marking the transition of the autumn season.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates in the western districts of Odisha, specifically Sambalpur and Phulbani, and is practiced by various Adivasi tribes including the Binjhal, Kuda, Mirdha, and Sama.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed during autumn festivals like Bhaijauntia, Phagun Puni, and Nuakhai, often to celebrate the season or to pray for the longevity of brothers.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by women who move to the rhythm of the music while shouting 'Dalkhai Bo!' at the start and end of song stanzas.
Male dancers participate by engaging in playful interaction with the women.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is provided by an all-male orchestra using the dhol, nisan, tamki, tasa, mahuri, flute, and dimki.
The dhol player dictates the tempo.
Listen for the dhol, nisan, tamki, tasa.
A percussion-heavy folk ensemble led by the dhol, featuring high-pitched calls and melodic accompaniment from the mahuri and flute.
